_notes: Shovel dig table: '0.384% each Vault Key 304/149 + Secret Garden Key, 0.24% SG Key variant' interpreted as VK304=0.384, VK149=0.384, SGK=0.24 (two game entries merged), VK233=0.144, VK370=0.048; sums to exactly 100.0.
Detector shovel: vault key total = 100 - 93.8 = 6.2%; distributed in shovel's 8:8:3:1 ratio → VK304=2.48, VK149=2.48, VK233=0.93, VK370=0.31.
Jack hammer: partial wiki data; table is confidence=inferred. No junk entries. Gems (2) = 39/176 = 22.159%; Wind-up Key = 3/176 = 1.705%; remaining coins fill to 100%.
Treasure map cells: A5→20, B6→26, B8→36, C8→37, D6→28, D9→43, E5→24, E8→39 (flat = (rank-1)*5 + col, letter A-E = col 0-4).
Car keys spawn rooms are taken from the wiki Locations line captured in tools/raw/wiki_item_locations.tsv, not from the digest, which named only the Garage.
Sanctum key: Reservoir (north) and Safehouse are areas, not rooms → in absent_spawn_areas.
master_key: classified kind=special_key; guaranteed_in is empty -- the Showroom sells it (shops.json tier_b, 80 coins), it is not placed in the room.
lock_pick_kit: darkroom/furnace/closed_exhibit/toolshed all exist in rooms.json → in spawn_rooms.

meta.notes: All three fabrication recipes are built and match the wiki (shovel+battery_pack+broken_lever->jack_hammer, sledge_hammer+battery_pack+broken_lever->power_hammer, compass+battery_pack->powered_electromagnet). On pickup, the Workshop's Dynamic Rarity is set to Standard or Unusual at 50/50 (room/options in the top-level battery_pack data section); the roll is deferred to the next hand dealt, where RNG is in scope. The second and later triggers in the same day do not re-roll -- they deterministically toggle to the other option (wiki: 'Triggering this effect multiple times in a day will always switch to the other one'). Trading Post is omitted: the wiki's Locations line lists it too, but the Trading Post's item flow is already modelled through its own trade/upgrade-disk channel, not the generic spawn pool.

coin_interest is read by effects/items/coin_purse.py, fired through special_items.py::on_coins_granted: each coin pickup adds to state.special.coin_interest, pays bonus for every whole per, and carries the remainder, which survives losing the purse. A held Lucky Purse wins COINS_GRANTED_PRIORITY outright, so the accumulator never advances beside it -- both as the wiki describes. Not modelled: the wiki's carry-over lockout, under which a Lucky Purse brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant makes the Coin Purse unobtainable that day. shops.py::fabricate consumes the recipe inputs with remove(consumed=True), and state.special.removed is day-scoped -- special_items.py::configure carries no contraption-component channel -- so the Coin Purse stays in the next day's pool.

mail_room is not a spawn_rooms entry: the wiki lists "Package" (a Mail Room delivery), not the Mail Room floor, and this sim already models that delivery via special_items.json's mail_packages (slot1 chains include compass). Commissary is also omitted: it is a shop-purchase room, already modelled through shops.json's commissary stock.

Fully built and tested: registered as ItemCapability.SHOP_DISCOUNT (amount=1) in engine/effects/items/coupon_book.py; shops.py's stock_for folds it via item_capability_sum and applies max(0, price-discount) to every stock entry AND the dynamically-appended showroom trophy; affordable is computed against the reduced price. See tests/test_shops.py::test_coupon_book_reduces_price_by_1 and ::test_coupon_book_floors_at_0. Nothing is missing; implemented was flipped to true on the strength of those two tests.

MAIN EFFECT built: the choice is over the FOUR RARITY LEVELS, not which Mechanical Room to target -- the room is whichever Mechanical Room (Room.is_category('mechanical')) was just drafted while the wrench is held; Game.choose detects the trigger and parks Phase.WRENCH_PENDING (engine/effects/items/gear_wrench.py; Game.can_set_wrench_rarity/set_wrench_rarity). The permanent choice is recorded in GameState.permanent_rarity / GameConfig.permanent_rarity, a SAVE-scoped dict carried by env/multiday.py::DayChain the same way axed_rooms is (survives the attempt wrap; NOT in DayChain._CARRYOVER_KEYS, which is bool-only). decks.py::build_decks consults cfg.permanent_rarity for the day-start bucket; Game.reset seeds state.dynamic_rarity from the same dict right after, so decks.py::set_dynamic_rarity/inject_rooms/inject_rooms_undealt/apply_upgrade agree on a wrenched room's bucket the rest of the day. Two things deliberately NOT built: (1) the wiki's separate pickup side effect (Workshop + Boiler Room -> Standard, that day) needs rng inside special_items._on_pickup, which takes none -- the same constraint battery_pack.py works around via a deferred pending-trigger resolved at the next deal; gear_wrench.py's own module docstring names this as a tracked gap. (2) The wiki also says the Conservatory writes this same permanent rarity slot and can reset a wrench-set rarity; this sim's Conservatory (decks.reroll_random_rarities) is a random DAY-SCOPED reroll of three undealt cards -- each moved card routes through set_dynamic_rarity so state.dynamic_rarity stays consistent with it for the rest of the day, but the reroll never touches the permanent record, state.permanent_rarity/GameConfig.permanent_rarity -- a known, deliberately-unfixed divergence from the wiki, not remodelled here.

Both published waivers are live in effects/items/hall_pass.py: an ItemHook.GEM_COST handler zeroes the cost of a hallway drafted from a hallway doorway, and an ItemHook.MOVE_STEP_COST handler zeroes a hallway-to-hallway move, both keyed on the shared _hallway_from_hallway test and on ItemCapability.FREE_HALLWAY_MOVES. Hall Pass sits first in both priority tuples, so a waived move never spends a Stopwatch charge or advances the Running Shoes counter. Not modelled: the wiki's guaranteed spawn, under which drafting the Guest Bedroom from the Cloister of Mila always puts a Hall Pass in it. guaranteed_in is empty, and cloister.py::mark_bedroom_bonus_item instead grants that Cloister's per-bedroom bonus as one ordinary extra pool draw at the bedroom's first entry, naming no item.

Rates, denominator, pity and pity_fail live on this record's lockpick effect and are read by special_items.py::_attempt_lockpick, which prefers the Pick Sound Amplifier when both tools are held; the door kinds match too (locks.py's DOOR_SECURITY is a separate segment kind no lockpick path touches). The rate ladder is indexed by state.special.lockpick_successes (successful picks today), matching "the chance goes down after a successful lockpick" / "after the first three successful lockpicks, remaining lockpicks have a 19/101 chance". state.special.lockpick_fails is the two-sided pity counter (+1/fail, -1/success): at >= pity it auto-succeeds and resets to -1; at <= pity_fail it auto-fails and resets to 1. The wiki gates the auto-fail case on lockpicking skill <= 20 -- lockpicking skill itself has no stat here (docs/experiments-design.md, permanent_lockpicking_skill), so this sim applies it unconditionally. NOT modelled: the per-door clause resetting the counter to 0 on a door already attempted (this sim tracks global per-day counters, not per-doorway, per _attempt_lockpick's docstring); the numerator bonus from lockpicking skill and its 98/101 cap; and its statement that building the Pick Sound Amplifier keeps this Kit out of the item pool on SUBSEQUENT days -- shops.py::fabricate marks recipe inputs consumed for the current day only.

luck_bonus is read by special_items.py::luck_bonus and added to effective luck wherever items are rolled (items.py::roll_ladder_count, items.py::_dowsing_effective_luck, and special_items.py's own spawn roll). The amount is this sim's own figure: the wiki calls the bonus a small amount and publishes no number for it, so the effect is directionally right but its size is unsourced. Not modelled: the wiki's carry-over lockout, under which a Lucky Purse brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant makes the Lucky Rabbit's Foot unobtainable that day. shops.py::fabricate consumes the recipe inputs with remove(consumed=True), and state.special.removed is day-scoped, so the foot stays in the next day's pool.

meta.wont_implement: puzzle-only effect; the sim has no document or lore layer and will not gain one
meta.notes: DECIDED never to build, not blocked. Its own effect reveals hidden text in documents, and this simulator has no document or lore layer -- nothing in engine/ reads lore or document text, and the assumed-solved doctrine means a puzzle a player enters is already solved. Its COMPONENT role is built and load-bearing: metal_detector + magnifying_glass -> burning_glass is the burning glass's ONLY source, and the burning glass is one of the two ignition tools, so this item keeps spawning in its 16 rooms. The wiki's Locations line also names Classroom, Commissary, Conservatory and Toolshed, all of which exist in rooms.json, plus the high-luck-only Den and Drawing Room; both tiers now carry the wiki's full list.

metal_detector_spawns is read by special_items.py::on_place, which rolls coins_chance and key_chance once each in the room just drafted -- luck-independent and never retroactive, both as the wiki has it. The two percentages are this sim's own; the wiki publishes no numbers for either. Three source claims are not modelled. The coin outcome always grants exactly one coin, where the wiki has the pile size depend on the room. The detection half -- the proximity beep that locates coins, keys and metallic tools, and the Powered Electromagnet suppressing it -- has no representation at all; special_items.py::grant auto-collects every spawned item, so locating one carries no decision. And the wiki's carry-over lockout is absent: a Detector Shovel or Burning Glass brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant should make the Metal Detector unobtainable that day while a Pick Sound Amplifier never does, but shops.py::fabricate consumes the inputs with remove(consumed=True) and state.special.removed is day-scoped, so the detector stays in the next day's pool.

shops.py::use_repellent consumes one can and bans the room the player stands in for shops.py::_REPELLENT_BAN_DAYS days; env/multiday.py::DayChain.advance decrements the counters and evicts the oldest ban once more than shops.py::REPELLENT_MAX_BANS are active, and decks.py::eligible_pool drops a banned floorplan plus its upgrade variants from the day's decks (outer-room drafting bypasses the decks, matching the wiki). NOT modelled: the wiki bars Repellent on most permanent and objective rooms, while shops.py::_REPELLENT_ILLEGAL_TARGETS names only entrance_hall, antechamber and room_46; the Foundation interaction (repelling The Foundation resets it out of the house and lets it be redrafted a week later, the wiki's only known way to move it); and the wiki's other guaranteed spawn, a Bedroom drafted from the Cloister of Mila -- only the Spare Bedroom (spare_bedroom__ix131) carries a guaranteed_in entry here, not its later upgrades or the Cloister-drafted Bedroom.

free_move_interval is read by effects/items/running_shoes.py, which waives the step cost of every n-th grid move and advances its own counter on every other one. It sits last in MOVE_STEP_COST_PRIORITY, so a Hall Pass or an active Stopwatch answers first and the counter does not advance -- matching the wiki's rule that a step loss already prevented some other way does not tick the shoes. The cadence itself is this sim's own rule. The wiki's rule is spatial rather than periodic: the position of the last step lost while holding the shoes is recorded, and a later step loss is waived only when the player is far enough from that position in euclidean distance, so walking back and forth between adjoining rooms never triggers the shoes at all, and no fixed number of moves guarantees a trigger. Also not modelled: the extra activation roll the wiki gives for entering anywhere outside the manor, with its own higher rates in the Gemstone Cavern, the Orindian Ruins and the Inner Sanctum. Area hops never consult the shoes -- game.py::travel_to deducts its area_hop steps directly, and special_items.py::move_step_cost is reached only from game.py::move -- so off the grid the shoes do nothing at all.

The dig_tool tag routes each dig spot at the cell through the shovel table in the top-level dig section (special_items.py::dig_all, which picks the best held tool by DIG_PRIORITY), covering the turnip outcome, the trash experiment trigger, and the Kennel's unlock-the-dug-room effect (the_kennel.py::unlock_dug_room, fired for treasure digs too). All three wiki recipes are in the fabrication table. Not modelled: the wiki's carry-over lockout, under which a Jack Hammer or Detector Shovel brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant makes the Shovel unobtainable that day, while a Dowsing Rod never does. shops.py::fabricate consumes the recipe inputs with remove(consumed=True), and state.special.removed is day-scoped -- special_items.py::configure rebuilds gated_out from cfg each morning and carries no contraption-component channel -- so a carried contraption leaves the Shovel in the next day's pool.

mail_room is not a spawn_rooms entry: the wiki lists "Package" (a Mail Room delivery), not the Mail Room floor, and this sim already models that delivery via special_items.json's mail_packages (slot1 chains include sleeping_mask).

spawn_rooms stays empty on purpose: the wiki's sole Locations entry (Clock Tower, plus Lost & Found which is excluded as already modelled through the room's own steal pool) is already covered by guaranteed_in. Also listing clock_tower in spawn_rooms would let the room's one-per-day random special roll sometimes 'spend' itself on a Stopwatch that was going to be guaranteed anyway, silently suppressing that day's chance for Clock Tower's other pool members (battery_pack, metal_detector, shovel, treasure_map) -- following the same guaranteed-only pattern already used by key_8 and basement_key.

The Telescope has two independent uses and BOTH are built in the engine, while this record itself is still inert. The Observatory arm (the item's own infobox description: a second independent night sky letting constellations activate twice) is wired: engine/game.py::can_view_night_sky asks effects/items/telescope.py::held for the extra per-Observatory sky, and nine of the thirteen constellations now activate (engine/constellations.py). blocked_on is consequently STALE -- what actually holds this record at implemented: false is that letting a tier-4 item into the spawn pool is an unmeasured change to the item economy, not a missing mechanic. The Planetarium arm IS built: Game.use_telescope_planetarium (engine/game.py) reveals one of the five planetarium_planets table below per day (Mora always last), each granting its payload permanently -- engine/effects/rooms/planetarium.py re-applies every unlocked payload on later days' placement/first entry. Not consumed by use. Gated out of the spawn pool at < 1 start-of-day star (engine/effects/items/telescope.py::gate, wired into special_items.configure()). guaranteed_in dropped: no wiki text supports a guaranteed Telescope on first Planetarium entry. spawn_rooms holds only loose-on-the-floor locations (owner ruling: obtainable-here is a separate concept from spawns-here, modeled elsewhere, and never added to spawn_rooms). Lost & Found and Trading Post are both wiki-listed telescope locations but are obtain-elsewhere channels, not floor spawns: Lost & Found already lists "telescope" in this file's own lost_and_found.pool, and Trading Post's tier-4 trade cycle already includes every tier-4 item generically (engine/shops.py::_roll_trade_graph, keyed on SpecialItem.tier) -- so both stay out of spawn_rooms rather than double-counting. The wiki's other two listed locations, Experiment and Spiral, are not rooms -- Experiment redirects to the Laboratory's unrelated Experiments mechanic, and Spiral is the Spiral of Stars, a 100-star secret constellation, not a room or area node -- so neither is added here either.

watering_can.py::on_pickup fills the can to its capacity param and watering_can.py::apply_on_enter converts one charge into one gem on entering a green room, wired in at special_items.py::_on_pickup and special_items.py::on_enter; on_enter runs once per room, which is the wiki's once-per-Green-Room limit. Refills are not modelled. The wiki also refills the can at the Kitchen tap once the Pump Room has flooded it, and at the Trading Post still after the endgame unlock; rooms.json gives pump_room and kitchen no effects, and nothing outside watering_can.py::on_pickup ever writes state.special.water, so a held can is worth at most capacity gems for the whole day. The book-tinting ability the wiki gates behind that same still is not modelled either.
Lost & Found is omitted from spawn_rooms: it is already modelled through the room's own steal-pool (special_items.json's lost_and_found table lists vault_key_370).

Granted from the pillar that emerges the first time the Antechamber is entered each day (guaranteed_in). Gates the well -> reservoir_south edge (basement_key_well, areas.json); not consumed on use, so it opens every basement door for the rest of the day and every later day.

spawn_rooms excludes garage: the Garage page says the Garage "does not usually contain special items lying around" -- the car (Car Keys' use site, /Usage) is not its spawn site. Locksmith is also omitted: it is a shop-purchase room, already modelled through its own stock/trade channel rather than the generic spawn pool.

Unlocking Key 8 (the Gallery art-naming puzzle) makes it appear in the Gallery every day rather than staying in the inventory. The sim assumes the player solves the puzzles of any room they enter, so the unlock and the find collapse into one guaranteed Gallery spawn - behaviourally the same check-in/check-out shape as the Coat Check.

Spawning and state are owned by engine/locks.py (locks.json keycard.source_rooms); excluded from the generic SPAWN pipeline (special_items.py::PIPELINE_EXCLUDED) to avoid double-spawning. Held on GameState.has_keycard rather than in the inventory, so every other subsystem reaches it through effects/items/keycard.py's held/grant/release: the Lost & Found steals it and the Trading Post trades it (tier 3, receivable per the wiki's bold tier-3 entry) through those accessors.
Obtainable today: the Showroom sells it for 80 coins (data/shops.json), via shops.py::buy.

A special-keys-menu row (Game.can_use_special_key_at_lock/use_special_key_at_lock), legal only while held and only at a locked door in a room carrying at least one of the five colours (Bedroom/Hallway/Green Room/Shop/Red Room -- effects/items/prism_key.py::fits; never a purely blue/black room). Using it colour-restricts the resulting draft to that room's colour (Game._deal_and_cache(colour=...), draft.py's colour gate), resolved without the Secret Passage's five-way COLOUR_PENDING player pick since the colour is never a player choice here. In the six rooms carrying more than one colour (the five Aquarium variants and the Maid's Chamber), the colour is one uniform rng draw (owner ruling: the wiki's 'chosen at random from all valid choices' taken literally over its reroll clause). Consumed on use and re-added to today's spawn pool the same day (remove(..., consumed=False)). NOT modelled: special key warping (a key used on a door with no following draft carrying its restriction to a later, unrelated draft elsewhere in the house -- this sim's LOCK_PENDING resolution always deals immediately) and the Silver Key's cross/t-layout bias combining with a Prism-Key-opened door (only one special-keys-menu row can be chosen per lock in this sim).

One of the game's eight Sanctum Keys, one per source room/area (see sanctum_key_vault, _clock_tower, _throne_room, _mechanarium, _music_room, _reservoir_north, _safehouse). Split from a single shared 'sanctum_key' id so each source's respawn can be gated independently once its key is spent (see GameConfig.collected_sanctum_keys) -- the same trap the Upgrade Disks hit under a single shared id. Owner ruling (docs/rooms.md): does not spawn at all until room46_reached; every source shares this gate. tier=5 and give-only (receive: false), like all eight Sanctum Keys and every other tier-5 item; the wiki tier-5 line carries no bold receivable markers. The tier-5 ring is vestigial: shops.py::_roll_trade_graph checks t5_special_chance (100 in shops.json) first and always substitutes the Allowance Token or the tradeable Upgrade Disk, so no tier-5 item resolves through the cycle. All eight keys are ONE game item at the Trading Post (wiki: each Sanctum Key is considered the same item, so holding several yields only one trade offer): shops.py::trade_offers collapses the family on the shared display name and offers the first held id in sorted order. Source shape: the wiki says Room 46 ALWAYS contains this key, so it is guaranteed_in room_46, not a spawn_rooms luck roll: room_46 has additional_max 0 (no luck-rolled items ever spawn there), and room_46 is an area node that travel_to reaches without ever calling roll_room_items, so a spawn_rooms entry there would never fire. Granted instead by special_items.py::on_area_arrival, which reads guaranteed_by_room generically on arrival at the room_46 area node. The room46_reached gate above already blocks it on the day Room 46 is first reached, matching the Crown's own wiki first-visit rule for the same room.

Granted only by opening Vault deposit box 370 with Vault Key 370 (special_items.json containers.vault_boxes); no generic spawn_rooms roll, since the box mechanism is the deterministic, already one-time-tracked source (used_vault_keys). Gated on room46_reached like every other source -- see sanctum_key_room_46.

Both inherited halves are live: dig_tool selects the detector_shovel table in special_items.py::dig_all, which prefers it over a held Shovel via DIG_PRIORITY, and metal_detector_spawns is read by special_items.py::on_place for the extra key/coin roll in the room just drafted. The table carries no turnip row, matching the wiki. Two source claims are not modelled. The on_place coin outcome always grants exactly one coin, where the wiki has the pile size depend on the room drafted. And the wiki's carry-over lockout is absent: a Detector Shovel brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant should make both the Shovel and the Metal Detector unobtainable that day, but shops.py::fabricate consumes the inputs with remove(consumed=True) and state.special.removed is day-scoped, so both components stay in the next day's pool.

The Dowsing Rod has nothing to do with colour. While held, it points at one of the three dealt floorplans on every deal/redraw (engine/draft.py's _pick_dowsing_slot, preferring a slot off data/items.json's dowsing_rod.avoid_rooms list); drafting that slot boosts that room's item spawn via its own system (engine/items.py's roll_dowsed_count), not the normal luck ladder -- see data/items.json's dowsing_rod table for the full published mechanics. Obtainable via fabrication (compass + shovel -> dowsing_rod). NOT modelled (named gaps): the Shelter interaction (a dowsed Lavatory/Furnace should count as sheltered; this sim's Shelter is a global day counter, not a per-room mark), the Coat Check/Compass quirk, real-time 'premature drafting' animation artifacts, and outer-room (West Path Shop) drafts.

Both inherited halves are live, but only one of them is in this record's effects. luck_bonus is read by special_items.py::luck_bonus; the coin doubling is registered in Python instead, as ItemCapability.COIN_MULTIPLIER plus an ItemHook.COINS_GRANTED handler in effects/items/lucky_purse.py, which sits first in COINS_GRANTED_PRIORITY and so supersedes the Coin Purse rather than stacking with it. Not modelled: the wiki's carry-over lockout, under which a Lucky Purse brought into a later day by Coat Check or the Moon Pendant makes both the Coin Purse and the Lucky Rabbit's Foot unobtainable that day. shops.py::fabricate consumes the recipe inputs with remove(consumed=True), and state.special.removed is day-scoped, so both components stay in the next day's pool.

Two of the wiki's breakable-wall locations are modelled: the Weight Room's south wall (engine/effects/rooms/weight_room.py::pull_south_lever, gated on power_hammer.held()) and the Grounds/Sealed-Entrance/Basement gate (engine/game.py::_gate_ctx's sealed_entrance_broken flag, also gated on power_hammer.held(); the wiki's two separate walls there -- the Grounds planks and the Sealed-Entrance/Basement wall -- are deliberately collapsed into this one flag, per that function's own docstring). Not modelled: the Greenhouse wall (breaking it drops Greenhouse's dead_end status for future dead-end counts on the wiki; rooms.json's greenhouse.layout stays static at 'dead_end' with no mechanic to change it), the Secret Garden's third valve (no valve/weathervane mechanic exists anywhere in the sim), the Precipice crack (its Castling Puzzle is auto-passed under the 'player solves every puzzle' doctrine rather than gated on this hint), and the Crate Tunnel's fourth-door wall. The Freezer wall is also not modelled by this item -- that gap is disclosed on upgrade_disk_freezer's own record instead (disk granted on first entry, bypassing the wall), noted here too since a reader of this record would not otherwise see it.

Robs the Locksmith on approach: auto-collects the 24 basic wall keys (four racks of 6; occasionally fewer) and disables both key purchase options for the rest of the day. The special key is NOT collected (special keys are never auto-collected). Built in shops.py: item.effect('locksmith_rob') sets state.shops.locksmith_robbed, which disables the key purchase rows. The drafting bias toward Mechanical Rooms plus the Rotunda (data/priority_draws.json category_biases 'electromagnet' entry) is driven by ItemCapability.ELECTROMAGNET in engine/effects/items/powered_electromagnet.py, not a data effect tag on this record. The room effect is modelled as an extra SPAWN, not a collection: special_items.py::on_place rolls one bonus coin and one bonus key for any held item carrying auto_collect, at the same 60/25 chances the Metal Detector's own metal_detector_spawns effect declares. The wiki gives the Electromagnet no extra resources at all -- it collects coins and keys already lying in a room, which items.py::grant_item hands over on entry here regardless of what is held -- so this record grants a Metal-Detector-sized bonus the source does not describe. Also NOT modelled: the wiki's rule that assembling this contraption leaves the Compass effect active for the rest of the day even if the Electromagnet is lost or never picked up, where ItemCapability.COMPASS_BIAS is read only while it is held; and its suppression of the Metal Detector's own detection while the two are held together.
Obtainable today: the Showroom sells it for 20 coins (data/shops.json), via shops.py::buy.

Obtainable today: the Showroom sells it for 30 coins (data/shops.json), via shops.py::buy. Its Tomorrow-Rooms bias IS live -- priority_draws.json's priority_draws list carries a Tomorrow Rooms (Chronograph) entry at the datamined 40%, matching the wiki's own framing ('This is a Priority Draw (40% for all Tomorrow Rooms)'): it fires once into slot 3 only, not as a per-slot category re-deal. draft.py::_active_conditions emits condition 'chronograph' while the item is held, checked via chronograph_active_from_state, which reads ItemCapability.CHRONOGRAPH (engine/effects/items/chronograph.py) rather than a data effect tag. Its other effect, REWIND, is now also live: after a redraw by any method, PendingDraft.rewind_stack holds every hand a redeal has replaced (Game._redeal_pending pushes there, unconditionally, before clearing); Game.can_rewind/rewind pop it back into the pending options for free and re-fire ON_HAND_DEALT, per the wiki ('activating effects that rely on drawing a floorplan') -- not a state restore, just a redraw whose output is pinned to a remembered hand. Free, unlimited, and one-way (owner ruling): rewind never pushes what it leaves, so it walks strictly backward to the original three floorplans and stops there. env/actions.py REWIND_ACTION (436) drives it; env/obs.py's prev_options key exposes the stack top so a policy can see what it would restore before acting.
Obtainable today: the Showroom sells it for 30 coins (data/shops.json), via shops.py::buy.

Obtainable today: the Showroom sells it for 50 coins (data/shops.json), via shops.py::buy. The wiki's first-draw-only restriction ('can be used any number of times, but only on the first draw. Redrawing floorplans causes both the drafting option and the visual model to vanish until the next draft') is not modelled: special_items.py::ornate_compass_active is a plain held-check, and game.py::_free_rotation_source grants a free rotation on every hand regardless of redraws -- game.py::_redeal_pending resets rotations_used to 0 on each redraw, re-arming the budget rather than disabling the source.

Not a colour-bias mechanic. Owner ruling 2026-08-12, which overrides the wiki: drawing a Red Room while drafting offers the option to filter it from ALL draws for the rest of the day; the player may take this once per hand, unlimited hands, gaining 1 gem and redrawing each time. There is no exemption -- not for colour-selective drafts, the Silver Key, the Prism Key, or ducts; the wiki's claim that blocked rooms remain obtainable by those routes is wrong. Matched with Room.is_category('red'), which yields 18, NOT the 13 rooms whose category field literally equals 'red' -- the five Aquarium-family rooms count as every colour. The filter lives in draft.py::room_draftable (the single gate every draw path passes through), keyed off SpecialItemsState.crown_blocked_rooms; it is a draw-time exclusion, never a deck removal or move, so deck sizes and the rarities they make legal are untouched. SpecialItemsState.crown_block_used tracks the once-per-hand spend and resets whenever a hand is dealt or redealt (draft.py::_fill_options), so a redraw's fresh hand re-offers it. Game.can_crown_block/crown_block are the player-facing API; env/actions.py CROWN_BLOCK_BASE (376..378, one id per option slot) drives them, and item_state[11] reports the running blocked-room count. Reachability: the wiki says Room 46 ALWAYS contains this, so it is guaranteed_in room_46 rather than a spawn_rooms luck roll -- room_46 has additional_max 0 and is an area node travel_to reaches without ever calling roll_room_items. Granted by special_items.py::on_area_arrival, which reads guaranteed_by_room generically. The wiki's 'It cannot be obtained the first time the room is reached, but is present in other times' is modelled by engine/effects/items/crown_of_the_blueprints.py::gate on cfg.room46_reached -- day granularity, so a second arrival on the FIRST day still grants nothing; the same convention the eight Sanctum Keys already use for this flag.

The Laundry Room key (same unmodeled Aquarium-drain mechanism) and the Tunnel key (Crate Tunnel, out of scope by standing ruling) are not modeled.

A contraption held at day start (carried overnight via Coat Check or Moon Pendant, rather than assembled fresh today) blocks a wiki-curated SUBSET of its own fabrication inputs (see the fabrication table above) from spawning/purchase/guaranteed-grant for that day. Wiki ("Effect" -> Interactions): "If a contraption is checked at the start of a day, it will remove some of its component items from the item pool to prevent multiple items with similar functionality from being obtained on the same day. The items removed differ from contraption to contraption." Every contraption blocks something -- no exemption: "The Dowsing Rod prevents the Compass from being obtained while checked" and "The Pick Sound Amplifier prevents the Lock Pick Kit from being obtained while checked" are both listed like every other entry. Not derivable from the fabrication recipe generically: most recipes block only ONE of their 2-3 inputs (wiki, verbatim): "Components not listed above can still be obtained while their corresponding contraption is checked. For instance, the Broken Lever and Battery Pack can still be found while either the Power Hammer or Jack Hammer is checked" -- Magnifying Glass is likewise never blocked. Each blocked id above is a real recipe input for that contraption in the fabrication table; the ones the wiki omits are not listed.

meta.notes: Tomb: near candles grant upgrade_disk_tomb + 4 dice; far candles reveal Diary Key — both pairs modeled as one ignition event granting all three (simplification: two-step reveal collapsed to one). Diary Key is a REWARD of lighting the Tomb, not a prerequisite. Chapel: lighting the altar grants accumulated Keeper of Tithes coins (chapel_tithes counter, incremented each time the entry -1 coin penalty actually fires); the payout is resolved in engine/special_items.py light(). Trading Post fuse grants (Upgrade Disk + 40 coins) are wiki-documented; the secret room is collapsed to an immediate grant since it is not modeled. Freezer thaw is temporary/daily and not modeled. Mine South ("area": true): lighting the eight candlesticks inside the Abandoned Mine (South) permanently lowers the stairway to the Precipice (engine/game.py::_gate_ctx sets the "candlestick_stairway_lit" flag from state.special.lit_targets, gating both mine_south<->precipice edges in areas.json); it has no grants here because the Upgrade Disk sitting in the mine is a separate, ungated pickup already granted on arrival by engine/special_items.py::on_area_arrival — granting it again here would double-pay. mine_south has no rooms.json record (it is an area-graph node, not a draftable room), so it is the one target keyed by an area id instead of a room id; "area": true marks that. absent_targets lists rooms/areas the wiki mentions that are absent from both rooms.json and this targets table (mine_south graduated out of it once the area graph modeled the node). Apple Orchard ("area": true): the wiki says an ignition tool scorches the sundial's base, the layers turn, and placing three microchips in the revealed holder unlocks the Satellite Dish permanent addition; "requires_items" (a dict of item id -> minimum held count) extends the older count-1 requires_item to a multi-item requirement, gating engine/special_items.py can_light()/light(). Any tool in the tools list above lights it. The wiki says "an ignition tool" without naming one; an owner play-report named the Burning Glass, and the owner ruled to trust the wiki, so the Torch lights it too. It has no grants here: lighting it sets the permanent GameState.satellite_dish_unlocked flag directly in light() rather than through the grants list, the same shape as mine_south's candlestick_stairway_lit flag, because the reward is a config unlock, not an inventory item or resource. Not reachable in play today: the sundial demands three HELD microchips, but the engine's microchip ceiling is two (day_start/vase_smash/doorstep/doorstep_dig, see the microchip record's meta.notes) -- the third microchip always sits in the Blackbridge Grotto pedestal, counted by the three_microchips area gate's counts_flag without ever being carried, so it cannot also satisfy this held-in-hand requirement. Built correctly and left unreachable, the same deliberate state as the pre-#210 three_microchips gate before the pedestal chip was modelled; no new chip source was added to close the gap. requires_item (singular, count-1) is supported by the engine but no target uses it (the Diary Key is a reward of the Tomb, not a prerequisite); requires_items (plural) is used by apple_orchard only.

Telescope's own SpoilerBox ("another use"): "The Telescope can be used in the Planetarium to permanently upgrade the room, unlocking a planet that confers permanent benefits to the room. Doing this does not consume the Telescope, but only one upgrade can be done per day." Both the Telescope and Planetarium pages carry the same five-planet gallery, verbatim: "The planets seem to appear in a random order, except Mora which is always last... Once all five planets appear, the Telescope can no longer be used in the Planetarium." Payload kinds: 'container' (Dauja spawns a Trunk -- containers.rooms has no static Planetarium entry, so engine/special_items.py's _planetarium_container_kinds overlays this generically, the same per-room-overlay shape as the Entrance Hall's trunk count); 'dig_bonus' (Veia -- the wiki's own Dig spots page, "Creating dirt piles": "1 dig spot will permanently appear in the Planetarium when activating one of the planet's effects using the Telescope", read as this specific planet's payload given the gallery's own Dirt Pile caption; modeled as +1 into state.special.veia_dig_bonus at the Planetarium's cell, the same generic per-cell overlay the Cloister of Veia and spread_dig_spots already share); 'food'/'dice'/'item' (Fennmora/Mamora/Mora -- an Apple, a single Ivory Die [dice resource, not the 4-dice Experiments effect], and a Prism Key, applied through the ordinary grants vocabulary special_items.apply_grant_list already resolves for containers and mail packages). Every unlocked planet's payload re-applies every later day (rooms/planetarium.py's ON_PLACE/ON_ENTER hooks), matching "permanent benefits to the room"; the day a planet is FIRST unlocked, engine/special_items.py::use_telescope_in_planetarium applies that one payload immediately since the room's own ON_ENTER already fired earlier that day.
